items.prompt: Ann and Ben have 72 stickers together. Ben has twice as many as Ann. How many stickers does Ann have?
hints: Draw one block for Ann.
Ben has 2 blocks. How many blocks in all?
Share 72 between the blocks.
items.explanation: Ann has 1 block and Ben has 2 blocks. That is 3 blocks in all. 72 / 3 = 24, so Ann has 24 stickers.

solution.say: Ann has 1 block and Ben has 2 blocks.

items.prompt: Tom has 3 times as many marbles as Jo. Together they have 64 marbles. How many marbles does Jo have?
hints: Draw one block for Jo.
Tom has 3 blocks. Together there are 4 blocks.
Share 64 between the 4 blocks.
items.explanation: Jo has 1 block and Tom has 3 blocks. That is 4 blocks in all. 64 / 4 = 16, so Jo has 16 marbles.

solution.say: Jo has 1 block and Tom has 3 blocks.

items.prompt: Ali and Budi have 100 stickers together. Ali has 30 more than Budi. How many stickers does Budi have?
hints: Take away the extra 30 stickers.
Then they have the same number.
Share what is left equally.
items.explanation: Take away Ali's extra 30: 100 - 30 = 70. Share equally: 70 / 2 = 35. Budi has 35 stickers and Ali has 65.

solution.say: Budi has 35 stickers and Ali has 65.

items.prompt: Three children have 90 cards in all. Ana has twice as many as Ben. Cat has as many as Ana and Ben together. How many cards does Cat have?
hints: Draw one block for Ben.
Ana has 2 blocks. Cat has 2 + 1 = 3 blocks.
Count the blocks in all: 1 + 2 + 3.
items.explanation: Ben has 1 block, Ana has 2 blocks and Cat has 3 blocks. That is 6 blocks in all. 90 / 6 = 15 for one block. Cat has 3 x 15 = 45 cards.

solution.say: Ben has 1 block, Ana has 2 blocks and Cat has 3 blocks.

items.prompt: I think of a number. I multiply it by 4 and take away 6. The answer is 30. What is my number?
hints: Work backwards from 30.
Undo take away 6 by adding 6.
Then undo the times 4.
items.explanation: Undo take away 6: 30 + 6 = 36. Undo times 4: 36 / 4 = 9. Check: 9 x 4 = 36 and 36 - 6 = 30.

items.prompt: Dina spent half of her money on lunch. Then she spent half of what was left on a book. She has Rp5.000 left. How many rupiah did she have at the start?
hints: Work backwards from Rp5.000.
Before the book she had twice Rp5.000.
Before lunch she had twice that.
items.explanation: After lunch she spent half of the rest, so the Rp5.000 left is half of Rp10.000. Rp10.000 is half of her money. So she started with Rp20.000.

solution.say: After lunch she spent half of the rest, so the Rp5.000 left is half of Rp10.000.
Rp10.000 is half of her money.

items.prompt: I think of a number. I triple it, add 7, and then halve the answer. I get 11. What is my number?
hints: Work backwards from 11.
Undo halving by doubling.
Then undo add 7. Then undo tripling.
items.explanation: Undo halving: 11 x 2 = 22. Undo add 7: 22 - 7 = 15. Undo tripling: 15 / 3 = 5. Check: 5 x 3 = 15, 15 + 7 = 22 and 22 / 2 = 11.

items.prompt: Rani is 6 years old. In 4 years Mum will be 3 times as old as Rani will be then. How old is Mum now?
hints: Find how old Rani will be in 4 years.
Rani will be 10. Mum will be 3 times that.
Mum will be 30 in 4 years. Go back 4 years.
items.explanation: In 4 years Rani will be 10. Mum will be 3 x 10 = 30 then. Mum is 30 - 4 = 26 now.

items.prompt: A father and his son are 50 years old together. In 5 years the father will be 3 times as old as his son. How old is the son now?
hints: Together they will be 10 years older in 5 years.
In 5 years their ages add up to 60.
The father is 3 times the son: that is 4 blocks.
items.explanation: In 5 years their ages add up to 50 + 10 = 60. Then the father is 3 blocks and the son is 1 block, so 4 blocks make 60 and 1 block is 15. The son will be 15, so he is 15 - 5 = 10 now.

solution.say: In 5 years their ages add up to 50 + 10 = 60.
Then the father is 3 blocks and the son is 1 block, so 4 blocks make 60 and 1 block is 15.
The son will be 15, so he is 15 - 5 = 10 now.

items.prompt: Ana has 20 sweets. She eats 3. Ben eats twice as many as Ana ate. How many sweets are left?
hints: Find how many sweets Ben eats.
Ben eats 2 x 3.
Take both amounts away from 20.
items.explanation: Ben eats 2 x 3 = 6 sweets. Together they ate 3 + 6 = 9. So 20 - 9 = 11 sweets are left.

items.prompt: A tank holds 50 litres. Tap A fills 4 litres every minute. Tap B fills 6 litres every minute. How many minutes do both taps need to fill the tank?
hints: Find how much the two taps fill in 1 minute.
4 + 6 = 10 litres.
How many 10s are there in 50?
items.explanation: The two taps fill 4 + 6 = 10 litres each minute. 50 / 10 = 5, so it takes 5 minutes.

solution.say: The two taps fill 4 + 6 = 10 litres each minute.

items.prompt: A snail climbs 5 m up a well in the day. At night it slips back 2 m. The well is 12 m deep. On which day does the snail get out?
hints: Find the height after each day and each night.
Day 1: 5 m, then slips to 3 m.
On day 3 it climbs from 6 m. Does it reach 12 m?
items.explanation: Day 1: climbs to 5 m, slips to 3 m. Day 2: 8 m, slips to 6 m. Day 3: 11 m, slips to 9 m. Day 4: climbs to 14 m and gets out. So it is on day 4.

solution.say: Day 1: climbs to 5 m, slips to 3 m.
Day 4: climbs to 14 m and gets out.

items.prompt: Ravi has 12 coins. Each coin is Rp500 or Rp200. Together they are worth Rp3.600. How many Rp500 coins does he have?
hints: If all 12 coins were Rp200, how much would he have?
That is Rp2.400. He has Rp1.200 more.
Each Rp500 coin instead of a Rp200 coin adds Rp300.
items.explanation: 12 coins of Rp200 make Rp2.400. Rp3.600 is Rp1.200 more. Each swap adds Rp300, so 1.200 / 300 = 4 swaps. He has 4 coins of Rp500.

solution.say: Each swap adds Rp300, so 1.200 / 300 = 4 swaps.

items.prompt: A farm has 10 animals. Some are rabbits and some are hens. Together they have 28 legs. How many rabbits are there?
hints: If all 10 animals were hens, how many legs would there be?
That is 20 legs. There are 8 more.
Each rabbit instead of a hen adds 2 legs.
items.explanation: 10 hens would have 20 legs. There are 28 - 20 = 8 more legs. Each rabbit has 2 more legs than a hen, so there are 8 / 2 = 4 rabbits.

solution.say: Each rabbit has 2 more legs than a hen, so there are 8 / 2 = 4 rabbits.
